items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: the bass notes are there and Costa’s, Don Costa’s chords to those songs, those ten songs, are so great.

ctx.x: Right. Somebody’s waiting to hit the bridge chords.

And my father goes, “no it’s not the bridge yet, you’ve got one more A section.” So the best thing is I’d say learn the songs and get them in your head. Or I learned a lot of them off records too. I found good records. You know the Sinatra records are great because, especially that “Sinatra and Strings” because the bass notes are there and Costa’s, Don Costa’s chords to those songs, those ten songs, are so great. Bass notes and chords are all there. And he was a guitar player so it all works. So that kind of…

What do you think of the kind of codified thing that’s happened in jazz — I get some younger students who come to me with this material they’ve had, and they ask me well when do I use this symmetric diminished scale? And I have to say jeez, I don’t even know what that is.
